tasks.spec:
You are fixing a robustness bug and one stale pin in freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. No network, no billed call, no uv: `export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp`, run `.venv/bin/python`. Do not git commit. YOU MAY EDIT: storygame/runtime/knowledge.py, storygame/runtime/item_facts.py, storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py, storygame/runtime/reveal_eligibility.py, tests/test_place_scoped_feed.py, tests/test_reveal_reach.py, tests/test_late_scene_repro.py. Never edit data/, bench/frozen/, docs/testing-runbook.md; do not reformat unrelated text. Shared runtime has NO story names.

BUG. Two recent generic features decide things from `world.together(protagonist, X)`: (1) the place-scoped narrator prompt (knowledge.py `_scene_frame` and `_within_reach` for committed statements; item_facts.py `_thing_names` scoping; cloudflare.py `_where_line`) and (2) the reveal reach gate (reveal_eligibility.py `explain_reveal` returning not_reachable). `together` is False whenever the protagonist has NO area (world.area(protagonist) is None, i.e. its parent is None/unplaced), which really happens (the narrator's item_facts left the protagonist unplaced twice in 109 live turns, and many unit-test states are never placed). In that state the prompt hides the whole scene (tests/test_3a_records_followup.py::test_records_are_grounded_and_shown_after_medical_entry_without_pre_reveal_contents fails: the records item vanished from THINGS) and every reach-gated reveal becomes unreachable.

FIX (fail open). When the protagonist's area is unknown (world.area(protagonist_id) is None), every one of those places behaves exactly as if the protagonist were with the scene: no prompt scoping (scene situation, committed statements, THINGS/PLAYER lists), no WHERE line, and the reach gate treats the reveal as reachable. Implement this once, in one small shared helper (for example in storygame/runtime/world_model.py or next to `_within_reach`; choose the least invasive place) and call it from all of those sites; do not duplicate the check. Behavior when the protagonist HAS an area is unchanged (the existing tests for scoping and reach must keep passing without modification).

TESTS FIRST. Add to tests/test_place_scoped_feed.py and tests/test_reveal_reach.py, small: (a) 1A with the protagonist unplaced (world.place or remove its parent so world.area is None; use whatever the existing tests in these files use to move it, then clear the parent): the narrator prompt equals the in-house prompt (scene situation present, house things listed, no WHERE line) and the card reveal is eligible; (b) a synthetic-story case in the same style as the file's existing synthetic cases. Also update tests/test_late_scene_repro.py: the expected place-form set for scene 1A (EXPECTED_PLACE_FORMS_BY_SCENE) must now include the new aliases that were added on purpose: for outside_house: outside, the yard, the driveway, the street, the curb, the front of the house; for mcgehee_home: inside, indoors. Read the test to find the exact normalized form it compares and add exactly the forms the failure output lists, nothing else, and say which.

FINISH: ruff format and ruff check every .py you touched; run the focused tests in the check (the full suite is run once at the end of the whole plan, not here); report what you changed.
